item.title: Europe’s big threat is not Trump and Putin redrawing the map. It’s our own learned helplessness | Natalie Tocci
item.description:
The US and Russia lack the power to impose their will on the continent – the Shenzhen summit was no Yalta 2.0

The first ever trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin was rich in symbolism and empty of substance. Many Europeans, filled with anxiety about the Chinese, Russian and US presidents potentially colluding, saw chilling echoes of the Yalta conference in 1945, when Joseph Stalin, Winston Churchill and Franklin D Roosevelt redrew the map of Europe.

But those – particularly in eastern Europe – who are fretting about another historic betrayal should remember that when it comes to European security today, we are the ones who hold most of the cards. Far more meaningful last week than Shenzhen was a gathering in Berlin, held at exactly the same time.

item.title: Burnham says it would be ‘unthinkable’ to rejoin EU without referendum
item.description:
Prime minister also says former Tory premiers who have criticised revival of Brexit debate are ‘stuck in the past’

Andy Burnham has said it would be “unthinkable” for the UK to rejoin the EU without holding another referendum, offering his strongest commitment yet to directly consulting the public if he concludes Britain should go back in.

The prime minister is planning to set out the long-term options for closer ties with the bloc next month, with concrete steps coming after the next general election, as he has pledged to stick to Labour’s manifesto red lines.

item.title: Burnham says it would be ‘unthinkable’ for the UK to rejoin the EU without a referendum – as it happened
item.description:
The prime minister’s remarks were the clearest commitment yet to not joining the EU without another vote

In her speech, Louise Haigh announced that Juergen Maier, chair of Great British Energy, has been appointed as the government’s northern economy and reindustrialisation commissioner. She said:

Giving business the confidence to invest here, and create good jobs in our industrial heartlands. Creating good quality jobs in all parts of the country. The role of the private sector is essential to fulfilling that. That is why I am delighted to announce today a new northern economy and reindustrialisation commissioner.

With an impeccable industrial career we can learn much from, welcome, Juergen Maier.
